newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN LEV FALLS TO 920-930 PER DLR AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN LEV FALLS TO 920-930 PER DLR AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 920-930 per dollat at the close from 910-915 in the morning and 885-890 at Thursday's close due to higher demand for foreign currency, dealers said.
"The market was very illiquid and dollar-bullish. Even demand for light dollar volumes instantly pushed the lev down," said a bank dealer.
High demand from banks and their clients pressured the lev as low as 950 in some deals in the afternoon, traders said.
Dealers said that turnover rose from Thrusday because more banks and clients built up dollar positions to hedge against an anticipated free fall of the lev next week.
Banks reported they bought and sold a total of $12.35 million on Thursday.
"The lev is likely to hit 1000 per dollar at the beginning of next week due to the ongoing political deadlock and the economic crisis," another trader said.
The lev traded at 737-738 on Monday, down from about 600 at the beginning of January.
